notes: Bundler-plugin route for Astro: Astro builds with Vite, but its Vite config lives inside astro.config, so the wizard installs @bugsee/vite-plugin and hands you the astro.config snippet (vite.plugins plus vite.build.sourcemap) instead of editing it. Astro does not load .env files while it reads astro.config, so process.env.BUGSEE_APP_TOKEN there needs the variable exported in the shell or CI (the build plugin also falls back to .env.bugsee-build-plugin from SDK 0.1.0-beta.7). The plugin reads the app token from BUGSEE_APP_TOKEN. From SDK 0.1.0-beta.7 the plugin also reads the token from .env.bugsee-build-plugin (the file the wizard writes); older SDKs need BUGSEE_APP_TOKEN exported. In CI, export BUGSEE_APP_TOKEN. The plugin does nothing without an app token. By default it deletes the .map files from the build output after a fully successful upload (deleteMaps: false keeps them), so they are not deployed. A build that pins script hashes with Subresource Integrity is warned about or refused, never silently broken. pnpm 11 approvals: the install script of the plugin's CLI dependency must be approved, and its name depends on the SDK (@bugsee/cli from 0.1.0-beta.7, @bugsee/bugsee-cli before), so both are written to allowBuilds; the one the project does not use is a harmless pre-approval and is removed again by uninstall.
verify: Verify symbolication in a production build: serve or deploy it (not the dev server), trigger a test error from it (for example a button that throws new Error('Bugsee test error')), then open the report in the Bugsee dashboard. The stack should show your original files, functions and lines; minified positions such as a.js:1:48210 mean the source maps were not uploaded for this build or do not match it.
